close_reason: Superseded by audit 2026-05-11. Composable-policy architecture already shipped: Profile -> ValidationPolicy -> verify_chain consuming SignatureVerifier + RevocationChecker callbacks. See pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:156-184. No ratification needed.
description:
**Keystone decision** for the verify pipeline. All other children (.2 through .20) reshape if this changes.

Survey of 7 reference implementations (OpenSSL, BouncyCastle, Microsoft CAPI, Apple Security, rustls-webpki, Go crypto/x509, mozilla::pkix) identified three architecture clusters:

1. **Big context + single call** (OpenSSL, Go) — legacy idiom.
2. **Build-then-validate, two calls** (BC, MS, webpki, Apple) — mainstream.
3. **Verifier state machine with caller callbacks** (mozilla::pkix) — purist.

Apple's composable-policy model is the recommendation: one policy object per concern (TLS-server-on-hostname, S/MIME-on-mailbox, revocation, lint), stacked, evaluated together. Production-validated 15+ years. Scales to new use cases without core API churn.

**Options:**

- **A) Ratify as proposed.** `VerificationPolicy` trait + `policies::*` constructor module + stacked-policies `verify()` signature.
- **B) Closed enum.** `VerifyPurpose::TlsServer{hostname}` etc. Simpler API; less extensible. Each new use case is an API addition.
- **C) Big context with flags** (OpenSSL-style). Avoid — bag-of-flags legacy idiom.
- **D) Two-call** (build path, then identity-bind in separate call). Avoid — ergonomics worse than Apple's composable model.

Decision-gate. Human label inherited from parent.
title: Ratify composable-policy architecture (keystone)
